decisions.reason: The same message independently adds sanitation and trapped-liquid requirements to this candidate; the electrical-isolation scope change requires no additional candidate update.
Service access is addressed by a separate clause and already has a complete same-message FOOD_SERVICE scope update; electrical isolation adds no further change.
Food-safe contact materials are independently introduced by the source message and are not changed by extending electrical isolation to food-service use.
The removable-whisk requirement receives its own same-message retail food-service scope update; liquid separation from electrical components does not alter its removal behavior.
The source decision concerns separation of liquids from electrical components, not the valve, flow, sequencing, or operator-control behavior of dispensing.
Electrical isolation does not change the spout's geometry, orientation, material, appearance, mounting location, or pour direction.
The spout seal preventing liquid from leaking into the base is a necessary part of keeping liquids separated from electrical components, so its applicability extends to the new FOOD_SERVICE context.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

The newest updates look great. Seeing the plumbing, drain routing, bowl integration, and full structure take shape has made me even more enthusiastic about the direction of the project.

While thinking about the future, I keep considering the possibility of eventually placing the Matcha Mixer in a retail setting if we decide to open a shop. For that reason, I’d like us to begin considering food-service and health department requirements now, while the machine is still at the prototype stage.

As development continues, I’d like to keep the following points in mind:

Food-contact materials such as stainless steel, food-grade plastics, food-grade silicone, etc.
Ease of sanitation and cleaning
Avoiding concealed spaces where liquid could collect or become trapped
Simple removal of the bowls, whisks, and other parts for cleaning
Keeping liquids separated from electrical components
Access for maintenance and servicing if a component ever requires replacement

When you have time, I’d also like to learn which materials are used wherever food contact occurs and whether you anticipate any areas presenting cleaning or sanitation difficulties.

Over the long term, I think retaining documentation for the following would be useful:

materials used
CAD files
wiring layout
cleaning procedures
exploded-view drawings if available

We don’t need all of that immediately, but if this develops into a larger project, that information could be extremely valuable. Everything looks fantastic overall, and I’m very excited to see the testing videos and completed assembly. It’s incredible to watch this go from an idea to a real machine.

[CLIENT_NAME_001] Burton

decisions.reason: Keeping liquids separate from electrical components does not alter the platform configuration, cup clearance, height, supported cup size, or footprint.
CAD retention is independently requested in the source message, while the electrical-isolation scope change does not alter the layout or CAD deliverable.
Liquid isolation does not change simultaneous load support, power-supply capacity, controller configuration, or overload margin.
The source decision does not change the prototype's standard 120V wall-power source.
The source establishes an isolation constraint but does not necessarily revise any listed BOM selection, compatibility rule, or artifact version.
